hints: Focus on what hot concentrated acidified manganate does to a C=C bond, it cleaves it completely and turns each alkene carbon into a carbonyl carbon.
Sketch the product HOOC-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH2-CH2-COOH and notice it has 7 carbons in one chain with two -COOH ends, so it must come from opening a 6-membered ring.
Work backwards by joining the two -COOH carbons back into a double bond and see where the methyl branch must sit on the original ring to give a 2-methyl pattern.
walkthrough:
**Recall oxidative cleavage**

Hot concentrated acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-$ breaks the C=C bond completely. Each $\text{C=C}$ carbon becomes a $\text{C=O}$ carbon.

Rule:
$$\text{R-CH=CH-R'} \rightarrow \text{R-COOH} + \text{HOOC-R'}$$

**Analyse the product**

The product is 2-methylhexane-1,6-dioic acid, $\text{HOOC-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$. It has 6 carbons in the main chain plus 1 methyl, total 7 carbons.

This matches the starting $\text{C}_7\text{H}_{12}$, so no carbon is lost. A cyclic alkene has been opened into a straight dicarboxylic acid.

**Reconstruct the ring**

For a dicarboxylic acid to form, both alkene carbons must have one H each, that is $\text{-CH=CH-}$. If one was $\text{C(CH}_3\text{)=}$, we would get a ketone, not a $-\text{COOH}$.

So the starting material must be a disubstituted cyclohexene, not a trisubstituted one.

**Locate the methyl group**

Join the two $-\text{COOH}$ carbons back together to reform the six-membered ring. The chain between them is $-\text{CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)}-$.

This means the methyl is on the carbon next to one end of the double bond. That is 3-methylcyclohex-1-ene, which opens to give the 2-methyl arrangement.

options.A: 3-methylcyclohexene has a -CH=CH- bond in a 6-membered ring. Cleavage gives HOOC-CH2-CH2-CH2-CH(CH3)-COOH, which is identical to 2-methylhexane-1,6-dioic acid when numbered from the other end. Both ends are carboxylic acids and the carbon count is correct.
options.B: 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene has a trisubstituted double bond, C(CH3)=CH-. Hot MnO4- would give a ketone at the more substituted end, forming 6-oxoheptanoic acid, not a dioic acid. Students choosing this forget the ketone versus acid rule.
options.C: 4-methylcyclohex-1-ene would also open to a dicarboxylic acid, but the methyl would be in the middle of the chain, giving 3-methylhexane-1,6-dioic acid, not the 2-methyl isomer. It is a position-isomer trap.
options.D: The dimethylcyclopentene has a 5-membered ring and a trisubstituted C=C bond. Cleavage would give a shorter keto-acid with a ketone at the C(CH3)= end, not a C7 dioic acid. Students choosing this miss both the ring size and the substitution pattern.
